import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a boxplot to visualize transaction amounts by type and fraud status
sns.boxplot(
    data=df, 
    x='transaction_type', 
    y='amount', 
    hue='is_fraud', 
    palette='Set1'
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amounts by Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(title='Is Fraud', loc='upper right', fontsize=12)

# Save the plot as a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a boxplot to visualize transaction amounts by type and fraud status
sns.boxplot(
    data=df, 
    x='transaction_type', 
    y='amount', 
    hue='is_fraud', 
    palette='Set1'
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amounts by Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(title='Is Fraud', loc='upper right', fontsize=12)

# Save the plot as a file
